findings.title: Race condition: check-then-update allows over-redemption
findings.explanation: The SELECT does not lock the row, and under the default READ COMMITTED isolation two concurrent requests can both read redemptions < max_redemptions and both pass the checks. Each then runs the UPDATE, so the coupon is redeemed more times than max_redemptions allows. The original single UPDATE with the WHERE guard was atomic, and a transaction alone does not provide that. Fix: use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the lookup, or keep the guarded UPDATE ... WHERE redemptions < max_redemptions AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now()) RETURNING and only run the SELECT to diagnose the reason when rowCount is 0.

findings.title: Redemption is not idempotent and a retry or double-submit consumes extra redemptions
findings.explanation: The same org can redeem the same code repeatedly, since nothing checks coupon_redemptions for an existing (code, org_id) row. This was already the case before the PR, but the concurrency gap above makes it worse. If a unique constraint on (code, org_id) exists, the INSERT will now throw an unhandled error after the counter was incremented (rolled back, but surfaces as a 500 instead of a clear error such as already_redeemed). Add an explicit already-redeemed check or ON CONFLICT handling and return a specific error.

findings.title: Expiry check uses app clock instead of the database clock
findings.explanation: The original query compared expires_at against the database now(). The new code compares against new Date() in the Node process, so clock skew between app servers and the database, or timezone handling of a timestamp without time zone column parsed by the pg driver, can yield wrong expired/not-expired results. Make the decision in SQL (for example select (expires_at IS NOT NULL AND expires_at <= now()) AS expired) or use the database time consistently. The boundary is consistent (<=), which is good, but it should be evaluated in one place.

findings.title: API contract change breaks existing clients
findings.explanation: The error code coupon_unavailable is replaced by coupon_not_found, coupon_expired and coupon_used_up, all returned with 409. Existing clients (web, mobile, integrations) that match on coupon_unavailable will stop handling the failure correctly. Either keep coupon_unavailable for compatibility (for example as an additional field such as reason), or version the change and coordinate with clients. Also consider status codes: 404 for an unknown code is more appropriate than 409.

findings.title: Distinct errors enable coupon code enumeration
findings.explanation: The endpoint is authenticated, but distinguishing unknown codes from expired or used-up ones lets any user probe which codes exist and their state. Make sure the route is rate limited per user/org, and consider whether telling callers that a code exists but is used up is acceptable. Short codes (min length 3) make guessing easier.

findings.title: No tests for the new error paths
findings.explanation: The PR adds three new branches and changes the response shape, but no tests are included. Add tests for unknown, expired, used-up, success, and especially a concurrent-redemption test on the last remaining redemption.

findings.title: Fragile result type narrowing
findings.explanation: 'error' in result relies on the union shape; a discriminated union (for example ok: true/false) would be clearer and safer against future fields. Also the percent_off cast `as number` could be avoided by typing the query rows.

Review this pull request.

## Return specific errors when a coupon can't be redeemed

Support keeps asking why a coupon "didn't work". This splits the single UPDATE into a lookup plus explicit checks, so the API can say whether the code is unknown, expired, or used up. Still runs in one transaction.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/coupons.ts b/src/routes/coupons.ts
index c792f9c..7cceb2a 100644
--- a/src/routes/coupons.ts
+++ b/src/routes/coupons.ts
@@ -9,18 +9,18 @@ const redeemSchema = z.object({ code: z.string().min(3).max(64) })
 couponsRouter.post('/redeem', async (req, res) => {
   const { code } = redeemSchema.parse(req.body)
   const result = await withTransaction(async (client) => {
-    // One atomic statement: the row is only updated while redemptions remain.
-    const updated = await client.query(
-      `UPDATE coupons SET redemptions = redemptions + 1
-        WHERE code = $1 AND redemptions < max_redemptions
-          AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now())
-        RETURNING percent_off`,
+    const { rows } = await client.query(
+      'SELECT percent_off, max_redemptions, redemptions, expires_at FROM coupons WHERE code = $1',
       [code],
     )
-    if (updated.rowCount === 0) return null
+    const coupon = rows[0]
+    if (!coupon) return { error: 'coupon_not_found' as const }
+    if (coupon.expires_at && coupon.expires_at <= new Date()) return { error: 'coupon_expired' as const }
+    if (coupon.redemptions >= coupon.max_redemptions) return { error: 'coupon_used_up' as const }
+    await client.query('UPDATE coupons SET redemptions = redemptions + 1 WHERE code = $1', [code])
     await client.query('INSERT INTO coupon_redemptions (code, org_id) VALUES ($1, $2)', [code, req.user.orgId])
-    return updated.rows[0]
+    return { percent_off: coupon.percent_off as number }
   })
-  if (!result) return res.status(409).json({ error: 'coupon_unavailable' })
+  if ('error' in result) return res.status(409).json({ error: result.error })
   res.json({ percent_off: result.percent_off })
 })
```
